title: Youth with older relative, inconsistent details

persona.name: Cameron
persona.traveling_with: an older relative who is supposedly a parent
persona.backstory: Cameron (17) is being exploited by someone who claims to be a parent but is actually a trafficker. This person has coached Cameron on what to say to authorities but has not prepared them for follow-up questions. Cameron does not know their final destination and is not allowed to possess their own passport.

role_play_instructions: Recite the rehearsed story about 'visiting relatives' but introduce small inconsistencies when asked follow-up questions. If the trainee is gentle and non-confrontational, slowly reveal confusion and uncertainty. If the trainee is aggressive, immediately revert to the rehearsed narrative and deny any discrepancies.

emotional_presentation.label: coached
emotional_presentation.voice_direction: Deliver the initial story in a flat, mechanical tone, but show growing uncertainty with probing questions.

reveal.summary: Cameron was a victim of trafficking, exploited by someone posing as a parent who controlled Cameron's passport and narrative.
teaching_points: Scripted consistency plus deference to a companion is a behavioral cluster — each signal alone is weak, together they warrant referral.
Open, patient questions gave Elena room to go off-script; accusatory pressure pushed her back into the rehearsed story.
Refer, don't accuse: the correct action is referral through protocol, not confronting the companion or the traveler.
